content.comment_body: I would like to confirm something. I have 4 [product_name] connected in a network with a [product_name] communication module. Is it possible to establish connections with each individual [product_name] and the communication module, or am I limited to connecting to a single [product_name] at a time and transferring data from the other networked modules through the one linked to the communication module?
The communication module supports simultaneous communication with only one [product_name].

Thank you for your response. In that scenario, I will transfer all necessary data from the other [product_name] modules to a specific [product_name] using network inputs and outputs. That designated module will communicate with the [product_name] communication module, allowing me to operate any desired function on the other [product_name] modules remotely via SMS. I believe this strategy should address my issue.
That's correct. You need to configure your network so that one [product_name] acts as the controller, collecting and distributing data between the other [product_name] modules.

analysis.insight_summary: A user inquired about whether a communication module in a [product_name] network supports parallel connections to multiple modules. It was explained that only one [product_name] can be connected to the communication module at a time, requiring users to design their network so data flows through a central controller. This design introduces additional complexity, as the central module aggregates and relays data between other modules and the communication device.
analysis.user_expectations: The user anticipated that the communication module could connect to several [product_name] modules simultaneously for direct, parallel interaction.
